definition: In this historical source, consciousness of freedom means the felt awareness of oneself as freely initiating action. It is treated as a prospective aspect of experience, pointing to novelty and self-activity rather than being fully explained by looking back at causes and past events alone.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Origin versus Nature; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not support the claim that “consciousness of freedom” means a “felt awareness of oneself as freely initiating action.” The text only mentions it as “evidence of a self-active intelligence in the world, which is not caused.”

The packet does support that freedom has a “prospective outlook” and is “prophetic of novelties,” but it does not explicitly frame this as “novelty and self-activity” from the standpoint of the subject’s own felt awareness.

The packet does not explicitly support the formulation “rather than being fully explained by looking back at causes and past events alone” in the way the definition states; it says freedom is “not adequately construed in terms of history,” but the provided definition’s paraphrase goes further than the quoted support.
